findings.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi results, which returns a dict keyed by node_id whose iteration order matches the requested keys only when all keys are found — when any node is missing, the surviving events are misaligned with their error_ids, producing ErrorEvent records with the wrong id. For a replay where one or more error events were nodestore-trimmed, every subsequent error log message in the LLM summary carries another event's title/message, and the timestamp used for chronological interleaving is wrong, silently corrupting the breadcrumb summary sent to Seer.

[BUG] The endpoint calls self.get_filter_params(request, project) and accesses filter_params["start"]/"end", but ProjectEndpoint's get_filter_params on a GET with no statsPeriod/date range falls back to project.date_added and now (or raises on invalid params), so a replay whose clicks occurred outside the default range yields an empty snuba response and error_ids silently become []. Replays older than the default window get summaries with zero error context even though error events exist; the user receives a degraded summary with no indication of the miss.

[BUG] process_raw_response is indexed with response[0] but query_replay_instance/process_raw_response can return an empty list (or a response shape whose rows list is empty) when the replay_id has no snuba row, causing IndexError and a 500 from the endpoint. A summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay not yet materialized in snuba (or deleted) crashes with a 500 instead of proceeding with empty error context, breaking the endpoint contract that previously only needed segments.

[ADVISORY] validate_timestamp and validate_age use self.initial_data.get(...) truthiness and cross-validate inside per-field validators, so a payload with timestamp=0 (falsy but serialized as an integer) plus age fails the intended exclusivity check in one direction, and both fields absent passes while the Working Draft requires one of them. Malformed browser reports with neither age nor timestamp (or timestamp=0) are accepted as valid and reach the metrics pipeline; future consumers assuming a valid timestamp get 0/None and misbehave.

[ADVISORY] The comment misspells 'segments' as 'segements' and the guard only checks max_segment_id, leaving the adjacent max_click_id branch (deleted elsewhere in the same function family) unguarded for the same null case — but since this diff only touches this site, the misspelling plus partial guard is a comprehension smell for the next maintainer extending null handling to click files. The next change adding null handling for click segment ids has to discover the parallel structure by reading a comment that already contains a typo, increasing risk of an asymmetric guard.

[BUG] src/sentry/preprod/__init__.py now does `from .analytics import *`, which executes at import of the sentry.preprod package; combined with the new analytics.py this runs analytics.register at import time, but the module-level registration is fine — however the wildcard import has no __all__ and re-exports nothing useful, so the package import chain now pulls in `sentry.analytics` for every preprod submodule import (including test collection of preprod API endpoints), adding import-time work; the actual defect is that organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py records the analytics event BEFORE the feature gate and before any validation failure path, so invalid/unauthorized requests still emit preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics. Operators watching the preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event see counts inflated by 403/feature-denied requests, and the event fires for requests that fail assembly, corrupting the funnel metric this diff was added to create.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is defined as a @staticmethod but calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title (the sibling class's private static), and it is invoked as self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) from GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow — this works, but _truncate_title lives on PRCommentWorkflow while get_environment_info lives on CommitContextIntegration, splitting the template helper across two classes in the hierarchy so any refactor of PRCommentWorkflow's truncation silently breaks the merged-PR path defined on CommitContextIntegration. A future move/rename of _truncate_title in PRCommentWorkflow raises AttributeError in get_merged_pr_single_issue_template at render time, breaking all suspect-PR comment posting with a 500 in the webhook/PR-comment task.

[ADVISORY] In update(), the owner handling branch runs before `condition_group = validated_data.pop("condition_group")`, so an update request missing condition_group (owner-only patch) raises KeyError on validated_data['condition_group'] paths below — the owner field was added as required=False but the surrounding update() assumes the full payload, so a partial PATCH carrying only owner cannot succeed. API clients attempting to PATCH a detector's owner without resending the full condition_group get a 500 (KeyError) or validation error, making the new owner field effectively unusable for partial updates.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi result values, misassociating error IDs with event payloads when any node is missing or returned in different order. nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict keyed by node_id; when one or more nodes are missing (expired/retention-deleted), dict.values() collapses and zip pairs the surviving payloads with the wrong event_ids, so the Seer summary and any downstream consumer attribute error titles/messages to the wrong error events.

[BUG] ErrorEvent.timestamp is read raw from the nodestore event payload (data.get("timestamp", 0.0)), which is an ISO-8601 string in stored event data, but is compared with '<' against breadcrumb numeric timestamps and used as a sort key. When the stored payload's timestamp is a string, error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"]) and the comparison in gen_request_data raise TypeError, so the summarize-breadcrumbs request 500s for any replay that has error events instead of returning the summary; the except in fetch_error_details does not cover this because sorting/comparison happens later.

[ADVISORY] Neither age nor timestamp is required, so a report containing neither field (or age=0, which passes the falsy .get("age") check in validate_timestamp) validates successfully, defeating the intended XOR enforcement between the Working Draft and Editor's Draft formats. Malformed browser reports pass validation and are counted in the browser_reporting.raw_report_received metric, polluting the sampling data the XXX comment says is being gathered for calibration; also age=0 with a timestamp is wrongly accepted as valid Editor's Draft format.

[ADVISORY] The new error-context behavior is gated on a raw query param enable_error_context with no corresponding feature/option entry, and the new query_replay_instance + nodestore fetch runs unconditionally even when disable_error_fetching is set. When enable_error_context=false the endpoint still executes the snuba query_replay_instance query and process_raw_response before discarding error_ids, adding an unnecessary per-request Snuba round trip; and the gate cannot be disabled org-wide without clients changing the URL param, so an incident on the new path requires a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The new branch taking error_events[0]['error_ids'] assumes process_raw_response returns a row containing error_ids for the requested field set, but the fields come from request.query_params.getlist('field'), which a client can set to anything (including empty), and this behavior is untested. A GET without a 'field' param (the common client shape for this endpoint, which previously never consulted query params for this purpose) exercises process_raw_response with an empty field list on the newly-added path; if that returns no error_ids key or empty rows the feature silently produces summaries with no error context, and no test in the diff covers the empty-field, no-error-ids, or replay-not-found edge cases for the new merge logic in gen_request_data.

[ADVISORY] get_condition_query_groups now indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] for groups derived from event_data.dcg_to_groups keys, while the dict is built from event_data.dcg_ids — two different key sets with no KeyError guard. If a DCG id appears in dcg_to_groups but not dcg_ids (e.g. a group entry persisted without its workflow linkage), the delayed-workflow task raises KeyError and the whole batch of delayed workflows fails to process, losing notifications for every workflow in that batch; the diff contains no test covering the divergent-key-set case for the newly-plumbed parameter.

[ADVISORY] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template silently drops the old {subtitle} (culprit) context and the new template is defined on CommitContextIntegration but truncation delegates to PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, coupling two classes with no test in the diff covering truncation or the environment suffix format. Issue titles longer than 50 chars (the common case for error titles) are cut mid-word with no unit test in the diff verifying the rstrip/ellipsis behavior or the 'in `env`' suffix rendering, so a regression in the merged-PR comment body (visible in customer GitHub/GitLab PRs) ships undetected; the old culprit subtitle context that end users relied on is removed with no acceptance criterion stating whether that loss is intended.

[ADVISORY] The PR is titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System' but the only replay-delete work present is a two-line null-guard in _make_recording_filenames; no bulk-delete endpoint, UI, task, or deletion API appears anywhere in the diff, so the stated deliverable is unimplemented in this changeset. Reviewers and release managers approve 'bulk delete' and ship a PR containing none of it; users still have no self-serve path to bulk-delete replays, and the missing feature surfaces post-merge as a product gap attributed to this PR.

[ADVISORY] The diff bundles an entire devservices overhaul (new snuba-metrics service, four subscription-results consumers, a new 'tracing' service profile) that is unrelated to replay bulk deletion. Unrelated infra changes ride along under a Replays PR title, so the devservices maintainers never review them and a bad consumer command or profile typo lands without the owning team's scrutiny.

[ADVISORY] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT flips from 'low' to 'off' (and the matching projectoption in projectoptions/defaults.py), changing default product behavior for autofix automation with no traceable requirement in a Replays bulk-delete PR. All existing projects relying on the implicit 'low' default silently stop running autofix on new issues after this merge; the product change is invisible to anyone reviewing under the Replays title.

[ADVISORY] Two previously-shipped migrations (0917 and 0920) are rewritten into no-op stubs, editing historical migration files rather than adding a new migration — and the neutralization is itself unrelated to the PR's stated intent. Any environment that already recorded 0917/0920 hits a migration checksum mismatch (or, on un-migrated envs, silently skips the conversion with only a comment explaining why), and the change ships hidden inside a Replays delete PR so nobody with migration context reviews it.

[ADVISORY] A full prompt-engineering rework of the feedback summaries LLM prompt (join separator, word/sentence limits) is included with no connection to replay bulk deletion. Behavioral change to a shipped AI feature lands unreviewed by the feedback-summaries owners; if summaries regress (e.g. raw feedback text no longer bullet-prefixed changes parsing downstream), the blame trail points at a Replays PR.

[ADVISORY] ParameterizationRegexExperiment is deleted and its option registration removed from options/defaults.py — a grouping-behavior change completely outside the stated Replays scope. Anyone running the 'grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent' sampled experiment (whose option is now unregistered) hits unknown-option errors or silently stops the experiment, and the grouping team never sees the removal.

[ADVISORY] The browser-reporting collector endpoint is rewritten from dataclass parsing to DRF serializer validation — a standalone API-validation overhaul with no relation to replay deletion. Ingestion behavior for browser reports changes (e.g. reports that previously passed dataclass construction now 422 on URL/choice validation) without the endpoint owners reviewing it, because it ships inside an unrelated PR.

[ADVISORY] The breadcrumbs-summarize endpoint gains a large error-context feature (Snuba replay query, nodestore fetch, interleaved error log messages, a new 'enable_error_context' query param) that is separate work from bulk delete and adds unpaginated per-request Snuba + nodestore calls. A new unauthenticated-consumer-visible query parameter and extra Snuba/nodestore round-trips land on every summarize request; if the feature has bugs (e.g. error_events zip misalignment when nodestore returns fewer rows than error_ids) they surface as production summarize failures attributed to a delete PR.

[ADVISORY] Detector validators gain owner (ActorField) create/update handling, plus a delayed_workflow slow-condition refactor and logger change — workflow-engine work with no traceable requirement in a Replays delete PR. Detector ownership semantics (owner_user_id vs owner_team_id assignment/clearing) change without workflow-engine review; a regression here breaks detector notifications/permissions and is invisible under the Replays title.

[ADVISORY] A new preprod analytics event plus its instrumentation in the assemble endpoint is bundled in, unrelated to the PR intent. The assemble endpoint now records analytics before the feature-gate check, so disabled-feature requests still emit events, skewing the new dashboard — and the preprod owners never review the placement.

[ADVISORY] A sweeping frontend refactor replacing styled FlexSpacer/FlexContainer divs with the shared Flex component across codecov selectors, event attachments, trace headers, and button chonk timing is included — pure UI churn unrelated to replay deletion. Visual regressions in core components (button elevation transition timing, layout of attachment tables, codecov selectors) land without frontend review, since the PR is reviewed as backend replay-deletion work.

[BUG] The new helpers get_environment_info and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template are defined on CommitContextIntegration but invoked as self.get_environment_info / self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template from GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow, which inherit from PRCommentWorkflow — a sibling ABC that holds a CommitContextIntegration as a constructor-injected collaborator, not a base class — so both call sites raise AttributeError when a merged-PR comment is built. Every merged-PR suspect-comment notification for GitHub and GitLab crashes with AttributeError instead of posting a comment; the new environment suffix never renders.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template references PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined as a staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration, so the lookup fails with AttributeError even if the method itself were reachable. Title truncation path is dead code that raises instead of truncating; any test or invocation reaching this line errors before formatting the comment.

[ADVISORY] get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() (a nodestore/DB fetch) once per issue inside the list comprehension in get_comment_body, an N+1 fan-out when a PR touches multiple issues. Building a single merged-PR comment for a PR with N linked issues performs N recommended-event lookups, slowing the webhook/comment path proportionally to issue count and increasing the chance the notification job times out.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs results with zip(error_ids, events.values()), but nodestore.backend.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id and can return fewer entries than error_ids when nodes are missing/expired, so positional zip mispairs the wrong nodestore payload with the wrong error_id and silently emits wrong titles/messages for the wrong errors. When any requested node is absent (expired retention, dropped node), every subsequent error event in the response carries another error's title/message, and the resulting summary sent to Seer describes errors that never happened in that order; should iterate by node_id lookup, not positional zip.

[ADVISORY] gen_request_data compares error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] (< event.get('timestamp', 0)) where the nodestore-sourced error timestamp (often a string in event payloads) is compared against breadcrumb event timestamps that may be numeric or string, so a mixed-type comparison raises TypeError inside the paginator's on_results callback rather than degrading to unordered output. A replay whose nodestore payloads store timestamps as strings while breadcrumb JSON events use numbers makes the whole summarize-breadcrumbs request 500 instead of producing a best-effort log list; the try/except in fetch_error_details does not cover this later comparison.

[ADVISORY] Removing ParameterizationRegexExperiment while keeping the ParameterizationExperiment type alias as a single-member union means any experiment registry entries still constructed from stored configs with the regex variant will fail to deserialize with no migration or fallback path shown in this diff. Deployments with persisted grouping-experiment configs referencing the regex experiment type crash or silently skip parameterization when the registry lookup no longer finds a matching class; the option key registration was also deleted (defaults.py), so any lingering options.get call on 'grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent' raises rather than returning a default.

[BUG] The original data-migration logic (converting org-level SavedSearches to GroupSearchViews) was deleted and replaced with `return`, silently abandoning the migration's stated purpose. On any environment where 0917/0920 have not yet run, the org saved-search conversion never executes; the replacement 0921 referenced in the comment is not present in this diff, so if it does not exist (or is not accepted in the same release), organization saved searches are permanently unconverted and users lose access to their org-level saved searches in the new views system — a data-loss-grade intent reversal with no human acceptance recorded.

[BUG] The revised migration body was gutted to `return` with a comment deferring to a 0921 migration not included in this diff. Deploying this PR alone means migrations 0917 and 0920 both become no-ops while no replacement has shipped, leaving org saved searches unconverted in every self-hosted/SaaS environment that has not already applied them — the rollback path (re-adding the logic) is also lost since the filter conditions (`visibility=ORGANIZATION, owner_id__isnull=False`) were deleted rather than moved.

[ADVISORY] The global default for `DEFAULT_AUTOMIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` (autofix automation) was silently flipped from "low" to "off" in a PR titled as a bulk-delete/replays change. Every project and organization relying on the default (no explicit project option set) stops running Autofix automatically on new issues the moment this deploys — a product-behavior objective change smuggled into an unrelated PR with no feature flag, options entry, or documented acceptance; the parallel change in src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205 makes it two places to keep in sync with no single source of truth.

[ADVISORY] The merged-PR comment format was rewritten mid-review: the culprit subtitle line was removed, a 50-char title truncation and environment suffix were added, and the bullet marker changed from `-` to `*`. Users of the GitHub/GitLab PR bot lose the culprit context (`subtitle`) that was the accepted format and instead get truncated titles plus an environment tag; because `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is a static method taking `title`/`url`/`environment` but calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` (defined on `CommitContextIntegration`), this also couples two unrelated classes, so any refactor of either class's method location silently breaks PR-comment rendering.

[ADVISORY] The `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` class was deleted and the experiment union collapsed to the callable variant only, removing a supported extension point. Any out-of-tree or sibling-PR code constructing `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` (e.g., grouping-config work) now fails at import, and the removal is coupled to deleting the `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` option in options/defaults.py — rolling-deploy skew means an old worker holding the option name in cache/set values hits an unknown-option error against the new defaults table.

[ADVISORY] The new browser_report_validation_failed warning writes the full raw report body (including the report's `url`, user_agent, and any tokens embedded in them) to logs on an unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt, CORS-enabled endpoint. Any anonymous web client can POST arbitrary report-shaped payloads and have their full contents persisted to Sentry's log pipeline; because CSP-violation reports routinely carry the page URL with query strings, an attacker (or ordinary traffic) will leak session tokens, PII-bearing URLs, and user agents into logs that are broadly readable by operators, expanding the exposure surface of any token-in-URL pattern.

[ADVISORY] The preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event is recorded before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature gate, so every authenticated request to the endpoint — including users of orgs where the feature is disabled or flagged off — emits an analytics record containing organization_id, project_id, and user_id. Operators analyzing the preprod_artifact.api.assemble event stream will count attempted accesses from orgs/users that were denied by the feature gate, conflating denied probes with successful assembly usage; anyone with analytics access learns which users are probing a private feature in which orgs.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow, so the method raises AttributeError the first time a merged-PR comment body is built. Every GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment with issues raises AttributeError instead of rendering the comment body; the PR bot comment feature breaks at runtime. This defect ships undetected because no test in the diff exercises get_comment_body end-to-end — the diff contains no test file touching this new template path (checked: no test/spec files appear in the diff at all), so the broken cross-class reference passes CI.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore.get_multi(node_ids).values(), so when any node_id is missing from the nodestore response the remaining values shift and each error id is paired with a different event's title/message/timestamp. The LLM summarizer receives error log messages attributed to the wrong event ids and wrong timestamps, producing summaries that reference errors the user never hit, or silently dropping errors after the first missing node. No test in the diff exercises fetch_error_details with a partially-missing nodestore result, so the misalignment is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness (self.initial_data.get("age")) and both fields are required=False, so a report containing neither age nor timestamp, or containing age=0/timestamp=0, passes validation despite the docstrings claiming each requires the other's absence. The Browser Reporting API collector accepts reports violating both the Working Draft and Editor's Draft timestamp semantics, and downstream consumers relying on one of the two fields get silently-empty timestamps. There is no test in the diff for the serializer (checked: no test files appear in the diff), so the 'validate each report' rewrite of the endpoint — a full switch from dataclass construction to DRF validation — ships with zero verification that valid reports pass and invalid reports return 422.

[ADVISORY] The new null-segment_id early return in _make_recording_filenames (the diff's stated bug fix) has no test asserting that a MatchedRow with max_segment_id=None produces [] instead of raising or generating bogus filenames. A future refactor of the bulk-delete filename generation can reintroduce the original crash (the comment says null segment_ids 'can cause this to fail') with no test failing; operators running bulk delete against replays with zero ingested segments are the ones bitten.

[BUG] An already-shipped migration's body is replaced with a no-op, so environments that already applied 0917 and environments that apply it fresh execute entirely different logic. Any environment that ran the original 0917 (e.g. self-hosted installs or long-lived staging databases, which do run migrations even if getsentry production claims it never did) has GroupSearchView rows converted with user_id=NULL for ownerless saved searches, while fresh environments record 0917 as applied without converting anything; the referenced replacement migration 0921 must now handle both partial states, and if it assumes a clean baseline the two populations of databases permanently diverge with no rollback for the already-converted rows.

[BUG] The already-shipped 0920 migration is gutted to a no-op with only a comment pointing at 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, which is not present anywhere in this diff. If 0921 is not actually added in this changeset, no migration performs the SavedSearch→GroupSearchView conversion at all, so existing ORGANIZATION-visibility saved searches are silently lost from the new views UI after the old read paths are removed — an unbackfilled data transition with no migration or rollback path; even if 0921 exists elsewhere, editing the shipped 0920 body (rather than adding a corrective migration) breaks the invariant that applied migrations are immutable.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against events.values(), assuming nodestore.get_multi returns results in the same order as the requested node_ids and with no gaps, so any missing node shifts every subsequent pairing and produces ErrorEvents whose id, title, message, and timestamp belong to different events. When a replay references an error event that has been trimmed from nodestore, every error after it in the list is silently attributed to the wrong event id/title in the summary sent to Seer — wrong data reported as success, no error surfaced to the user or logs (the outer except only fires on raised exceptions, not misalignment).

[BUG] fetch_error_details catches every exception (including nodestore backend failures and get_multi timeouts) and returns [], so the endpoint returns a 200 breadcrumb summary with all error context silently dropped. A nodestore outage or per-event error yields a 'successful' AI summary that omits the errors the user asked to be summarized; the only signal is a Sentry event, and the end user has no way to know the error context is missing.

[BUG] error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x['timestamp']) compares nodestore event timestamps against segment event timestamps (event.get('timestamp', 0)) that may be of different types, raising TypeError when a nodestore timestamp is an ISO string (or when a segment event lacks a timestamp and defaults to 0). A replay whose stored error event carries a string timestamp (nodestore event payloads store timestamp in varying formats) makes gen_request_data's comparison `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)` raise TypeError, returning a raw 500 from an endpoint whose other validation paths return clean 4xx/404 responses.

[ADVISORY] query_replay_instance's Snuba response is indexed with response[0] and .get('error_ids', []) with no handling for a malformed or field-less response, so the error-context feature silently no-ops when the query omits the error_ids field. If the request's `field` param (forwarded verbatim from request.query_params) doesn't include error_ids, the endpoint returns a successful summary with zero errors and no log or user-visible indication that error context was dropped — the operator tuning the endpoint sees no signal to debug.

adjudication.rationale: In `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the new code explicitly guards indexing: `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", []) if response else []`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] validate_timestamp and validate_age use self.initial_data.get(...) truthiness and cross-validate inside per-field validators, so a payload with timestamp=0 (falsy but serialized as an integer) plus age fails the intended exclusivity check in one direction, and both fields absent passes while the Working Draft requires one of them. Malformed browser reports with neither age nor timestamp (or timestamp=0) are accepted as valid and reach the metrics pipeline; future consumers assuming a valid timestamp get 0/None and misbehave.
matched_golden_ids: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: using self.initial_data.get(...) with truthiness causes timestamp=0 (and potentially age=0) to be treated as absent, breaking mutual-exclusion/required-field validation. It explicitly calls out timestamp=0 being falsy and leading to incorrect exclusivity/acceptance behavior, aligning with the golden comment’s concern about presence detection needing a key-existence check ('timestamp' in initial_data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In update(), the owner handling branch runs before `condition_group = validated_data.pop("condition_group")`, so an update request missing condition_group (owner-only patch) raises KeyError on validated_data['condition_group'] paths below — the owner field was added as required=False but the surrounding update() assumes the full payload, so a partial PATCH carrying only owner cannot succeed. API clients attempting to PATCH a detector's owner without resending the full condition_group get a 500 (KeyError) or validation error, making the new owner field effectively unusable for partial updates.

adjudication.rationale: In `BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update()` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py), the new optional `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` is handled conditionally, but the method still unconditionally does `condition_group = validated_data.pop("condition_group")`. The added tests for owner updates always pass `self.valid_data` (which includes `condition_group`), so this edge case is not covered and the code path remains unsafe for owner-only updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi result values, misassociating error IDs with event payloads when any node is missing or returned in different order. nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids) returns a dict keyed by node_id; when one or more nodes are missing (expired/retention-deleted), dict.values() collapses and zip pairs the surviving payloads with the wrong event_ids, so the Seer summary and any downstream consumer attribute error titles/messages to the wrong error events.

[BUG] ErrorEvent.timestamp is read raw from the nodestore event payload (data.get("timestamp", 0.0)), which is an ISO-8601 string in stored event data, but is compared with '<' against breadcrumb numeric timestamps and used as a sort key. When the stored payload's timestamp is a string, error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"]) and the comparison in gen_request_data raise TypeError, so the summarize-breadcrumbs request 500s for any replay that has error events instead of returning the summary; the except in fetch_error_details does not cover this because sorting/comparison happens later.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), `ErrorEvent.timestamp` is set directly from `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` without normalization. Later, `get_request_data` sorts via `error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])` and `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. If the nodestore event payload’s `timestamp` is not numeric (e.g., a string), this will raise a `TypeError` during sorting or comparison, causing the endpoint to 500. The `try/except` in `fetch_error_details` won’t catch this because the failing sort/compare happens after it returns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Neither age nor timestamp is required, so a report containing neither field (or age=0, which passes the falsy .get("age") check in validate_timestamp) validates successfully, defeating the intended XOR enforcement between the Working Draft and Editor's Draft formats. Malformed browser reports pass validation and are counted in the browser_reporting.raw_report_received metric, polluting the sampling data the XXX comment says is being gathered for calibration; also age=0 with a timestamp is wrongly accepted as valid Editor's Draft format.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer`, both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, so a report containing neither field will validate successfully and be counted in `browser_reporting.raw_report_received`, contrary to the intent of supporting exactly one of the two spec variants. Additionally, the mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")`) rather than key presence, so edge values like `0` can bypass the XOR validation (e.g., `timestamp=0` and `age=0` would not trigger either validator and would validate).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new error-context behavior is gated on a raw query param enable_error_context with no corresponding feature/option entry, and the new query_replay_instance + nodestore fetch runs unconditionally even when disable_error_fetching is set. adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code always executes `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to compute `error_ids` before checking `enable_error_context` (parsed into `disable_error_fetching`). When `enable_error_context=false`, it correctly skips `fetch_error_details` (nodestore fetch), but it still performs the Snuba query + response processing and then discards the result by setting `error_events = []`. Also, the new behavior toggle is only via the raw query param `enable_error_context` and the diff shows no org-wide option/feature flag to disable this path operationally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new branch taking error_events[0]['error_ids'] assumes process_raw_response returns a row containing error_ids for the requested field set, but the fields come from request.query_params.getlist('field'), which a client can set to anything (including empty), and this behavior is untested. A GET without a 'field' param (the common client shape for this endpoint, which previously never consulted query params for this purpose) exercises process_raw_response with an empty field list on the newly-added path; if that returns no error_ids key or empty rows the feature silently produces summaries with no error context, and no test in the diff covers the empty-field, no-error-ids, or replay-not-found edge cases for the new merge logic in gen_request_data.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the new error-context path derives `error_ids` from `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist('field'))` and then `response[0].get('error_ids', [])`. Because `fields` is client-controlled, a request that supplies `field` values that don’t include `error_ids` could cause `error_ids` to be omitted and silently disable error-context injection (`error_events=[]`), which is an edge case not explicitly covered by the new tests. However, the finding misstates the code as `error_events[0]['error_ids']` (it doesn’t), and the “no `field` param” / empty-field-list path is in fact exercised by the added tests (`test_get_with_error` calls `self.client.get(self.url)` without `field` and asserts error text is included).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] get_condition_query_groups now indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] for groups derived from event_data.dcg_to_groups keys, while the dict is built from event_data.dcg_ids — two different key sets with no KeyError guard. That means the dict keys are derived from the same `event_data.dcg_ids` set as the `dcg.id` values being indexed, so the claimed KeyError due to `dcg_to_groups` vs `dcg_ids` divergence isn’t supported by what this diff shows. (If anything, this change reduces the prior risk where the helper used `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The breadcrumbs-summarize endpoint gains a large error-context feature (Snuba replay query, nodestore fetch, interleaved error log messages, a new 'enable_error_context' query param) that is separate work from bulk delete and adds unpaginated per-request Snuba + nodestore calls.
